title: What happens to the mean when every value changes?
description: Eleven values have a mean of about seven point one eight. The board then adds ten to every value, subtracts one from every value, and doubles every value, and finds the new mean each time. Keeko's doubt is that doubling every value adds two to the mean.
teaching_notes: One idea: adding or subtracting the same number shifts the mean by that number, and multiplying every value multiplies the mean by that number. Watch for students who add the multiplier to the mean instead of multiplying the mean.

video_script.why: The child sees that changing every value in the same way changes the mean in the same way, without finding the sum again.
video_script.substitution: Find the mean once, then shift it by the same number when every value is shifted, and multiply it when every value is multiplied.
video_script.anchor: eleven values written in a row, with their mean marked below and arrows for add ten, subtract one and double
video_script.wrong_answer: doubling every value adds two to the mean
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko thinks doubling every value adds two to the mean. But the sum doubles from seventy nine to one hundred and fifty eight while the count stays eleven, so the mean doubles too.
video_script.payoff_line: The mean is about seven point one eight

final_answer.value: About 7.18, then 17.18 after adding 10, 6.18 after subtracting 1, and 14.36 after doubling
final_answer.spoken: about seven point one eight, then seventeen point one eight after adding ten, six point one eight after subtracting one, and fourteen point three six after doubling

hold_back: Answer: About 7.18, then 17.18 after adding 10, 6.18 after subtracting 1, and 14.36 after doubling
never_show: the final answer line before the answer beat
maths_rules: every value doubled: new sum = 158; 158 / 11 = 14.36 = 2 x 7.18
video_script.design: One idea: shifting every value shifts the mean, and doubling every value doubles the mean. The row of values stays from ground to the end of the idea part. Wrong idea: doubling adds two to the mean.
